segment_1.topic_phrase: what changes when the driver who hit you had been drinking
segment_1.setup: I'm **{{INTERVIEWER}}**, and today we're getting into crashes caused by a driver who had been drinking, and what actually changes about your case when that's what happened.
segment_1.credential: **{{ATTORNEY}}**, your firm handles a lot of different injury work, and crashes caused by impaired drivers are the ones you go deepest on.
segment_1.prompt: Someone was just hit by a drunk driver. Lay out what makes their case different. And if you've a real-world example, take us through it.

attributes.name: Tried a drunk driving case
attributes.detail: Cases you took to a jury, and what a jury does once it hears the driver had been drinking.

attributes.name: Impaired driver crashes
attributes.detail: Not injury cases generally. Crashes caused by a drinking driver, how many, and how recently.

attributes.name: License, checkable
attributes.detail: Your license and disciplinary record, and where anyone can go to confirm it.

attributes.name: Two cases, one client
attributes.detail: The county court, the judges, and how the prosecution and your client's claim run alongside each other here.

attributes.name: Running beside the prosecution
attributes.detail: How you use what the state develops without letting your client's claim wait on it.

attributes.name: Proving impairment
attributes.detail: Everything you stack on top of the test result, because a defense lawyer will go after that number by itself.

attributes.name: Records behind the test
attributes.detail: What you secure in the first days, including the maintenance and calibration files sitting behind any reading.

attributes.name: Toxicology and reconstruction
attributes.detail: The people who explain what the driver's condition actually meant at the moment of impact.

attributes.name: Finding coverage
attributes.detail: How you get to every policy that could pay when the driver carries little or nothing.

attributes.name: Clocks that don't wait
attributes.detail: The two-week medical window and the filing deadline, and why neither one pauses for the criminal case.

attributes.name: What it costs
attributes.detail: The percentage, whether it rises if you file suit, who pays for the toxicology work, and what happens if you lose.

attributes.name: Why the bar claim fails
attributes.detail: Why a claim against the place that served the driver almost never works here, and why you tell people that up front.

questions.q: What makes a case different when a drunk driver caused the crash in Stuart?

bullets.label: There's a second case running
bullets.detail: the criminal case moves on its own schedule and your claim doesn't wait for it.

bullets.label: The case can be worth more
bullets.detail: when a driver made the choice to drink and drive, a jury can award things they would never award after an ordinary crash.

bullets.label: Where it happens here
bullets.detail: late nights on US 1 and Kanner Highway, and on I-95 and the Turnpike, where the speeds turn one bad decision into a life-changing crash.

questions.q: Does a criminal conviction settle your injury case?

bullets.label: It helps a lot on fault
bullets.detail: a conviction makes it much harder for the other side to argue the driver was being careful.

bullets.label: It doesn't set the number
bullets.detail: how badly you were hurt and what it costs you still have to be proved on their own.

bullets.label: Don't wait for it
bullets.detail: the state's case moves through the Martin County courthouse on its own schedule, and the evidence for your claim goes cold in a matter of weeks.

questions.q: Can you sue a drunk driver in Florida even though it's a no-fault state?

bullets.label: Yes, once the injury is serious enough
bullets.detail: no-fault pays the first bills, and past that point you can go after the driver directly.

bullets.label: It changes how they treat you
bullets.detail: the same claim an insurer would grind down after an ordinary crash, they take seriously here.

bullets.label: Your own coverage still matters
bullets.detail: a lot of the drivers on I-95 and the Turnpike are from out of state and insured somewhere else, so the coverage on your own car is often what pays.

questions.q: What makes an injury serious enough to sue over in Florida?

bullets.label: There's a line
bullets.detail: ordinary soreness gets handled by your own insurance, and it's crossing that line that lets you go after the driver.

bullets.label: Permanence is the test
bullets.detail: an injury you'll carry, a lasting loss of something your body used to do, or scarring that doesn't go away.

bullets.label: It's proved with records
bullets.detail: the doctor who treated you and the imaging are what establish it, not how you describe it.

questions.q: How is it actually proved that the driver was drunk, in Stuart and across the Treasure Coast?

bullets.label: It's layered, not one number
bullets.detail: the breath or blood result, what the officer saw, and how the car was being driven.

bullets.label: A lot of it's in the report
bullets.detail: the long form report gets filled out on any serious injury, and the officer's own observations of the driver are in it.

bullets.label: Where they were before
bullets.detail: the places out along US 1 and Kanner Highway, where nobody walks home, they drive, and they drive fast.

questions.q: How reliable is the breath test, really?

bullets.label: It's one machine
bullets.detail: the state uses a single instrument statewide, and it has to be maintained and calibrated on a schedule.

bullets.label: The paperwork is checkable
bullets.detail: the maintenance and calibration records can be demanded, and gaps in them matter.

bullets.label: It'sn't the only proof
bullets.detail: the blood work, the officer's observations and what the driver was doing all stand on their own.

questions.q: What happens when the driver refused the breath test?

bullets.label: Refusing isn't a clean escape
bullets.detail: the refusal can be shown to a jury, and juries don't think much of it.

bullets.label: Blood can still be taken
bullets.detail: with a court order, and in a serious crash that's a normal step.

bullets.label: The rest of the case doesn't need it
bullets.detail: the driving, the witnesses and the hospital records tell the story without a number.

questions.q: How does the crash report help an injury claim in Stuart?

bullets.label: It captures the first account
bullets.detail: it gets written by Stuart Police, the Martin County Sheriff's Office, or the Highway Patrol, depending on which road you were on.

bullets.label: It usually stays out of court
bullets.detail: the report itself is generally kept out at trial, so the case gets rebuilt from what's underneath it.

bullets.label: It still drives the number
bullets.detail: the adjuster reads that report long before anyone files anything, and it sets where they start.

questions.q: Can you sue the bar that served the driver in Stuart?

bullets.label: Almost never
bullets.detail: Florida is one of the strictest states in the country on this, and most claims against a bar go nowhere.

bullets.label: There are two openings
bullets.detail: serving somebody underage, or serving somebody the bar knew had a serious drinking problem.

bullets.label: Which one comes up here
bullets.detail: the places out along US 1 and Kanner Highway, where nobody walks home, they drive, and they drive fast.

questions.q: Why is it so hard to hold a bar responsible in Florida?

bullets.label: The law was written narrowly
bullets.detail: most states let you sue a bar for overserving an adult, and Florida doesn't.

bullets.label: The exceptions are real but small
bullets.detail: underage service, and service to someone known to be habitually addicted.

bullets.label: It changes where you look
bullets.detail: with the bar out, the search moves to every policy behind the driver, and out here that regularly means a policy written in another state.

appendix_question_bank.question_text: If I was hit by a drunk driver in Florida, what makes my case different from an ordinary crash?
How does a drunk driving conviction turn ordinary negligence into negligence per se under Florida law?
Can I actually sue a drunk driver in Florida even though we are a no-fault state?
What is Florida's serious injury threshold and why does it decide whether I can sue for pain and suffering?
How is the driver's intoxication actually proven in my civil case?
What is the Intoxilyzer 8000 and how reliable is breath-test evidence in Florida?
What does Florida's implied consent law mean for the driver who refused a breath or blood test?
How does the Florida traffic crash report support an injury claim against a drunk driver?
Can I sue the bar or restaurant that served the drunk driver who hit me?
Why is Florida's dram shop law one of the narrowest in the country, and when does it actually apply?
How do punitive damages work in a Florida drunk driving case, and why does intoxication unlock them?
Is there a cap on punitive damages in Florida, and when can that cap be exceeded?
What is my drunk driving accident case actually worth in Florida?
How are medical bills, lost wages, and future care calculated in a serious DUI crash claim?
What happens if the drunk driver who hit me has no insurance or only minimum coverage?
How does my own uninsured and underinsured motorist coverage protect me against a drunk driver?
Does Florida PIP cover me after a drunk driving crash, and where does it fall short?
When can I bring a bad-faith claim against an insurer that refuses to pay fairly?
How does the drunk driver's criminal DUI case affect my separate civil injury claim?
What is criminal restitution, and is it enough on its own to make me whole?
How does a case change when a drunk driving crash causes a DUI manslaughter charge?
Who can file a wrongful death claim when a drunk driver kills a family member in Florida?
How long do I have to file after HB 837 cut Florida's deadline to two years?
Can the drunk driver's lawyer still blame me, and how does Florida's 51% comparative negligence rule work?

outro.signoff: That's all we've for this one. **{{PODCAST_NAME}}**. We will see you next time.
